**Paper Engines: The Age of Mechanical Calculators**
*May 10 to October 4, 2026*

Before silicon, there were gears, levers, and brass. *Paper Engines* traces the century when inventors taught machines to count and changed how people did business and science.

Eighty-five calculating machines fill the galleries, from desktop curiosities to the rugged workhorses of banks, railways, and observatories. The centerpiece is an 1851 arithmometer, one of the earliest calculators made commercially, used by clerks and engineers across Europe. Its stepped drum mechanism is still crisp after more than 170 years, inside a polished wooden case.

Turn a crank and read the result. You will see how these machines worked, who built them, and why their makers believed arithmetic could be automated.
